rubric.scope: Private technology companies raising $500K–$15M (with tolerance band to $16.5M)
rubric.not_for: Due diligence, portfolio management, technical merit evaluation

section.name: Evaluation Context
section.block: This is a two-profile Ideal Company Profile (ICP) scoring instrument built for a fundraiser to use as a top-of-funnel qualification and prioritization tool. Its purpose is to evaluate private technology companies (software, AI/ML, developer tools, cybersecurity, defense/dual-use, fintech, health tech, climate tech) that are actively seeking capital in the $500K–$15M range and produce a structured, scored assessment of each company's probability of successfully closing a funding round. This instrument is not a due diligence tool and was not designed for technical merit evaluation or investment decision-making. It scores fundraising velocity and investor appetite, not product quality, code quality, architectural elegance, or engineering merit.

The rubric is explicitly built to identify companies that can raise money most easily — not companies with the best technology or most promising products. Technical promise and fundraising ease diverge meaningfully in practice. The evaluation target is investor psychology, deal velocity, and capital market dynamics. Every criterion, weight, and scoring band is calibrated against this objective. STANDING INSTRUCTION: The objective is fundraising velocity and investor appetite — not technical promise. Score accordingly.

block.name: Client Specifications
block.revision_note: Tech v2.0 R1: Softened the Team Priority "strong preference for halo-employer alumni" language to expressly acknowledge the non-traditional founder equivalences operationalized in A1/B1 (Change C / R3), preventing an internal contradiction between this design-brief spec and the broadened "or equivalent" criteria. No other Block 1.3 text was altered; the solo-founder protocol reference and the Cap Table spec are unchanged.
block.spec: Series A (100%), Seed/Pre-Seed+ (85%), Pre-Seed below $500K with no institutional participation (excluded)

Single most important criterion at Profile B (Seed/Pre-Seed+). Strong preference for halo-employer alumni, repeat founders, and technical founders with research-lab or frontier-lab pedigree — with non-traditional founder equivalences (deep vertical-domain operator experience, academic/research standing, and authentic open-source leadership) expressly recognized under the A1/B1 "or equivalent" qualifying criteria, so that this preference is not read as halo-employer-only. Solo founders accepted with profile-specific penalty per A1/B1 solo-founder protocol.

Sporadic or messy cap tables are a hard disqualifier across both profiles. Founder ownership below 10% post-Seed, stacked SAFEs above $3M with no priced round in 24+ months, and IP not assigned to the company are additional hard disqualifiers per Section 2.3.
Preferred but not a hard requirement.

Software-appropriate IP expectations: patents weighted at zero or slight-negative for pure software companies (research convergence: Feld, Wilson, Lemley; post-Alice empirical evidence). Patents and trade secrets weighted heavily for hardware, deep-tech, defense, and biotools companies via application notes. Moat-buildability trajectory replaces moat existence as the primary Profile B signal.

section.block: The $500K–$15M range is split into Profile A ($3M–$15M) and Profile B ($500K–$3M) to create meaningful separation between two genuinely different fundraising environments. Because no universal regulatory stage applies across technology companies, the rubric uses three routing inputs simultaneously: (1) raise size, (2) development stage selected from the enumerated taxonomy in Section 2.1, and (3) investor composition characterized by the four-tier classification in Section 5 Block 1. The development stage taxonomy serves the dual function that FDA regulatory stage serves in LS v5.1 (anchor for routing logic plus primary product viability signal context); it is operationalized in Section 2.1 and applied through the Product/Traction Evidence criterion (A3/B3).

Tech v1.0 R1: Two-track INFORMATION-SCARCE vs. INFORMATION-ABSENT classification transferred from LS v5.1 v5.0 R4 with mechanism preserved exactly. Tech-specific observable-signal lists per criterion (D1a/D1b of the Design Brief) replace life-science signal lists. The "highest-predictive, lowest-observable" problem is more acute in tech than in life science because key predictive metrics (Net Revenue Retention, Burn Multiple, cap table specifics) are structurally non-public; a founder-attestation-by-band protocol is added in this section to handle these criteria. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE for the tech-specific signal lists — additional cases are needed to validate that the SCARCE/ABSENT distinctions function correctly across the five business models covered by the rubric.
When information for a criterion is insufficient to produce a confident score, assign the midpoint of the applicable scoring band and flag the score with [INSUFFICIENT DATA]. Do not penalize companies for missing information below the midpoint. This protocol applies to all criteria in both profiles. The Data Confidence indicator in Section 5 aggregates these flags to provide an overall assessment of score reliability.
MIDPOINT-DEFAULT JUSTIFICATION STANDARD: When the midpoint-default is applied to a criterion, the Justification field must do more than cite protocol application. The evaluator must articulate why the midpoint — rather than a score above or below midpoint within the band — is appropriate given whatever partial evidence exists. If partial evidence supports a score above or below the midpoint, score accordingly and document the partial evidence. Reserve the exact midpoint for situations where evidence is genuinely absent and no directional signal is available.
INFORMATION-SCARCE vs. INFORMATION-ABSENT CLASSIFICATION:
Before applying the midpoint-default to any criterion, the evaluator must classify the missing information as one of two types:
INFORMATION-SCARCE: Evidence exists that the company has engaged in the activity measured by this criterion, but the details are not publicly disclosed. The existence of the underlying activity is supported by some observable signal, even if specifics are not available. When information is SCARCE: apply the midpoint-default. Flag as [INSUFFICIENT DATA — INFORMATION-SCARCE]. In the Justification field, state the observable signal that confirms the underlying activity exists.
INFORMATION-ABSENT: No evidence exists that the company has engaged in the activity measured by this criterion. The absence is not caused by non-disclosure of existing information but by the non-existence of the things the information would describe. When information is ABSENT: score in the lowest applicable band per the band definitions. The midpoint-default does not apply. Flag as [INSUFFICIENT DATA — INFORMATION-ABSENT] and document in the Justification field: (a) what evidence was searched for, (b) why the absence is classified as information-absent rather than information-scarce, and (c) the specific band assigned and its justification.
AMBIGUOUS CASES: When partial evidence exists but it is ambiguous whether the underlying activity has occurred, default to INFORMATION-SCARCE and document the ambiguity. The INFORMATION-ABSENT classification should only be applied when the evaluator has actively searched for evidence of the underlying activity across available sources and found none.
TECH-SPECIFIC OBSERVABLE SIGNALS — INFORMATION-SCARCE (activity exists but details not disclosed): A1/B1 Team Quality: Founder has confirmed employment history with any halo or relevant employer; LinkedIn profile shows active history; product was shipped (implying a team built it). A2/B2 Market and Sector: Company has a website; product addresses an identifiable market; sector classification can be assigned from product description. A3/B3 Product/Traction Evidence: Product is live (website, app store presence, GitHub repo); customers exist (logos, case studies, testimonials); fundraising has occurred (round announcements, Crunchbase data). A4/B4 Capital Efficiency: Round size disclosed; employee count observable (LinkedIn); time since last round known. A5/B5 Cap Table: Investor names disclosed; accelerator membership disclosed; lead investor identifiable; some terms inferable from round structure. A6/B6 Moat: Product is live and addressable; competitive landscape inferable; moat claims may or may not be articulated publicly. A7/B7 Exit Pathway: Sector inferable; acquirer universe assessable from named strategic acquirers in past M&A activity (independent of company).
TECH-SPECIFIC TRIGGER CONDITIONS — INFORMATION-ABSENT (underlying activity does not exist): A1/B1 Team Quality: No employees confirmed on LinkedIn; founder LinkedIn profile non-existent or unverifiable; founder identity uncorroborated by third-party sources. A2/B2 Market and Sector: No website or website does not describe a product or sector; pre-product status confirmed by absence of any product description. A3/B3 Product/Traction Evidence: No GitHub activity (no code shipped) for software companies; no app store presence for consumer; no website with product page; zero customer references in any source; zero press coverage. A4/B4 Capital Efficiency: No fundraising disclosed and no documented capital history (founder cannot attest to capital raised because none has been raised). A5/B5 Cap Table: No investor names disclosed and no founder attestation possible (company has no investors). A6/B6 Moat: No product live and no articulated moat thesis (pre-product company with no public materials). A7/B7 Exit Pathway: Sector is so novel that no acquirer universe can be defined (extremely rare).
FOUNDER ATTESTATION PROTOCOL FOR HIGHEST-PREDICTIVE, LOWEST-OBSERVABLE SUB-COMPONENTS:
Certain sub-components of the highest predictive value are structurally non-public in technology companies (Net Revenue Retention, Burn Multiple, founder ownership percentage, SAFE stack total). The rubric accepts founder attestation by band as a valid scoring input for these sub-components, subject to the following protocol:
NRR (A3 Profile A): Founder attestation by band (≥120%, 110–120%, 100–110%, <100%) accepted as primary scoring input. Refusal to attest moves the score to the lower portion of the applicable band, not midpoint. Founder attestation flagged INFORMATION-SCARCE in Data Confidence.
BURN MULTIPLE (A4/B4 when revenue exists): Founder attestation by band (<1×, 1–1.5×, 1.5–2×, 2–3×, >3×) accepted. Refusal triggers INFORMATION-SCARCE flag.
CAP TABLE SPECIFICS (A5/B5 — founder ownership, SAFE stack total): Founder attestation by band (founder ownership: >50%, 30–50%, 15–30%, <15%) accepted. Refusal to attest at A5/B5 is itself a negative signal moving score to the lower portion of band and is also a contributing condition to the cap table integrity disqualifier when refusal is paired with other ambiguity signals.
DATA CONFIDENCE AGGREGATION: When two or more criteria carry INFORMATION-SCARCE flags driven by founder-attestation-only signals, the aggregate Data Confidence rating moves to MODERATE. When four or more criteria carry such flags, the rating moves to LOW. This calibration matches LS v5.1 §5 Block 4 Data Confidence rating definitions and applies in parallel to those definitions: an evaluation may carry MODERATE Data Confidence via the founder-attestation aggregation rule even when total INSUFFICIENT DATA flag count would otherwise suggest HIGH.
DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENT: When founder attestation is the primary scoring source for any criterion, the Justification field must state explicitly: "Founder attestation by band [stated band]; INFORMATION-SCARCE flag invoked." Silent reliance on founder attestation without disclosure is not permitted.

Any deviation from the client's original specifications in the scoring criteria, weights, or band definitions must be documented in a Market Context Note at the point of deviation. The evaluator has latitude to adjust, reorder, replace, or add criteria relative to the original specifications, provided deviations are disclosed.

Both profiles score on a base scale of 100 points. The combined AI Modifier and Market-Evidence (M&A) Modifier on the Sector criterion (A2/B2) can adjust the total by up to ±2 points, producing a scoring range of 98–102 points. Fundability tier thresholds are defined in absolute point values and apply across the full scoring range. The 96–102 envelope of LS v5.1 is preserved in form; in tech v1.0, the operative envelope is 98–102 because the combined-modifier cap of ±2 governs all sector-criterion adjustments. See Section 3 A2 and Section 4 B2 for the cap mechanism and Section 5 Block 3 modifier sub-block for output documentation.
DESIGN CONSTRAINT: This instrument uses an additive, independent-criterion scoring architecture. When a single development (such as a strategic pivot, key person departure, or regulatory event) affects multiple criteria simultaneously, the independent scoring structure cannot express the correlated risk quantitatively. Evaluators should describe cross-criterion risk correlations qualitatively in the Top 3 Fundability Risks (Block 5) and Fundraising Outlook (Block 5) sections of the output. The quantitative scores for each criterion remain independently assessed per their respective band definitions.
CROSS-CRITERION SYMMETRY: When a single risk affects multiple criteria and appears in multiple Top 3 Fundability Risk entries in Block 5, each risk entry must note the correlation to the other affected criteria. A cross-criterion risk described from only one direction understates its aggregate impact on the evaluation.

section.name: Routing Logic
section.block:
Every company evaluated under this instrument must first be routed to Profile A or Profile B. Routing is based on three required inputs: (1) the company's target raise size; (2) the company's development stage selected from the enumerated taxonomy below; and (3) the company's investor composition characterized by the four-tier classification defined in Section 5 Block 1. The routing decision is made before any criterion is scored. Omission of any routing input is a format error.
DEVELOPMENT STAGE ENUMERATED LIST (Software/Software-AI primary): Pre-Product — research, prototype, or demo only; no shippable product. Pre-Revenue Closed Beta — live product with limited access (alpha or closed beta); no commercialization motion. Pre-Revenue Public Beta or Public Release — product live and accessible; no paying customers. Commercial Pre-Revenue — product live with design partners or LOIs; no booked ARR. Commercial Early Revenue — booked ARR present but below $500K, or below $1M for AI-native applied. Commercial Scaling Revenue — ARR between $500K and $3M (or $1M–$3M for AI-native applied). Commercial Series A+ Revenue — ARR above $3M, structurally aligned with Series A graduation thresholds. Growth Stage — ARR above $10M; structurally above the upper ceiling of this instrument.
HARDWARE / DEEP-TECH / DEFENSE / SPACE SUPPLEMENTARY STAGES (applied in parentheses when relevant, with application notes on affected criteria per Section 2.2): Pre-Hardware — concept, IP only. Prototype — working hardware, uncertified. Pre-Certification — production-grade hardware awaiting certification. Certified, Pre-Revenue — certified, no contracts booked. Contracted Revenue — active government, DoD, or strategic contracts (for defense/dual-use).
Assign to Profile A if the company's target raise is $3M–$15M inclusive. Profile A companies are typically at Commercial Early Revenue through Commercial Series A+ Revenue stage with institutional Series A lead engagement and formal board governance. Profile A expects evidence of unit economics, named institutional lead investor, experienced operating teams with halo-employer pedigree or prior founding experience, and institutional-quality cap tables. Where development stage and investor composition suggest Series A regardless of disclosed raise size (e.g., bridge round at $3M off a prior Series A), Profile A applies.
Assign to Profile B if the company's target raise is $500K to under $3M. Profile B companies are typically at Pre-Product through Commercial Scaling Revenue stage with Seed-stage micro-VC lead, accelerator-anchored, or angel-syndicate composition. Profile B expects strong team and founder-market fit signals, emerging traction or design-partner validation, accelerator tier signals as anchor lead-investor proxies, and clean SAFE-based or priced-seed cap table structure.
Companies targeting $2.5M–$3.5M fall in the gap between profiles. Resolve routing using the secondary inputs: if development stage is Commercial Scaling Revenue or above ($500K+ ARR, or AI-native applied equivalent) AND investor composition reflects institutional Series A lead engagement → Profile A. If development stage is Commercial Pre-Revenue, Commercial Early Revenue (below $500K ARR), Pre-Product, or earlier AND investor composition is Seed-stage micro-VC, accelerator-anchored, or angel syndicate → Profile B. If routing is ambiguous within the gap range (e.g., bridge round with mixed signals), conduct a split evaluation under both profiles and report the score range, mirroring LS v5.1 §2.1 gap protocol.
Companies with target raise below $500K but with at least one institutional participant (named VC fund or Tier 1/2 accelerator per Section 3 A5 / Section 4 B5 accelerator tier classification) are routed to Profile B with an information-scarce flag. Companies with total raised under $275K and no institutional participation are classified Out of Scope — Pre-Seed Exclusion per Section 2.2.

Tech v1.0 R2: Scope boundary structure transfers from LS v5.1 §2.2 with three modifications. The upper ceiling and tolerance band mechanism is preserved with tech-specific values ($15M ceiling, $16.5M Gray Zone, above $16.5M Out of Scope — Benchmark). A pre-seed exclusion floor is added at the lower end ($275K with no institutional participation = Out of Scope — Pre-Seed Exclusion). A Hardware/Deep-Tech/Defense/Space Profile Limitation scope boundary is added analogous to LS v5.1 HD-1a, signaling that hardware-intensive companies are within general scope but evaluated via application notes. An AI-Native Frontier Fund-Mandate-Fit scope boundary is added to address companies whose raise sizes ($50M–$2B+) structurally exceed the primary audience's check capacity even when otherwise high-scoring.
The instrument is calibrated for private capital markets. Publicly traded companies and pre-seed companies (total raised under $275K with no institutional participation) are OUT OF SCOPE. An OUT OF SCOPE flag is a scope/instrument mismatch, not a disqualifying deficiency. Out-of-scope companies may be evaluated as benchmark exercises if clearly flagged.
Companies whose target raise is $15M or below are IN SCOPE. Companies whose target raise exceeds $15M but is at or below $16.5M (10% above the $15M ceiling) are classified as GRAY ZONE. Gray Zone companies are evaluated under Profile A with a mandatory Gray Zone scope flag in the output. The evaluator must note the overshoot in the Routing Rationale and acknowledge that the instrument's calibration may be less precise for raises above $15M. Companies whose target raise exceeds $16.5M are OUT OF SCOPE and may only be evaluated as benchmark exercises with an Out of Scope — Benchmark flag.
Companies with target raise of $500K or above are IN SCOPE under Profile B. Companies with target raise below $500K but with at least one institutional participant (named VC fund or Tier 1/2 accelerator) are IN SCOPE with information-scarce flag, routed to Profile B. Companies with total raised under $275K (Carta 2025 median post-money SAFE) AND no institutional participation are classified OUT OF SCOPE — Pre-Seed Exclusion. Pre-Seed Exclusion evaluations may proceed as benchmark exercises with an Out of Scope — Benchmark flag.
The instrument is calibrated for software-primary and software-AI-primary technology companies with revenue-stage, user-growth, or open-source community signals as the dominant product viability anchors. Hardware-intensive companies — including pure hardware, robotics, physical AI with hardware dependence, deep-tech with capex requirements, defense/dual-use with government contract revenue, and space/aerospace — are within the general scope of the instrument but produce persistent band language friction, most notably on A3/B3 (Product/Traction Evidence, where certification milestones and government contract revenue replace ARR), A4/B4 (Capital Efficiency, where Burn Multiple tolerance is relaxed and capex/grants/debt funding replaces pure equity), A6/B6 (Competitive Moat, where patents and ITAR/EAR-protected IP function as practical patent equivalents), and A2/B2 (Market Opportunity, where Defense/Dual-Use, Robotics/Physical AI, and Space/Aerospace tier classifications apply).
The v1.0 hardware application notes embedded within A2/B2, A3/B3, A4/B4, and A6/B6 collectively provide an analog framework for evaluating hardware-intensive companies. This framework is a documented boundary condition of the instrument, not a rubric deficiency. Evaluations of hardware-intensive companies conducted under this framework remain valid but carry lower rubric fit than evaluations of software-primary companies. Evaluators must document the hardware classification in the Block 1 Market Context Note field, identify which criteria required analog application via application notes, and note that rubric fit limitations apply.
Clients whose target pipeline exceeds approximately 20% hardware/deep-tech/defense/space companies should consider commissioning a dedicated Profile C track calibrated to hardware fundability signals — including certification milestones, government contract revenue, capex/grants/debt funding structures, manufacturing-process power as moat, and 7–12 year exit timelines. See Future Revisions entry FV-tech-1 for the deferred Profile C design direction. Until such a track is developed, hardware-intensive companies continue to be evaluated under the analog framework with the boundary condition flagged in the Market Context Note.
Companies classified AI-Native Frontier per A2/B2 — research-lab pedigree (ex-OpenAI, ex-Anthropic, ex-DeepMind, ex-FAIR, ex-Meta AI, ex-Mistral, ex-Cohere senior research roles), proprietary training compute or training data, foundation-model-or-equivalent development, raising at $50M+ valuations — frequently operate at raise sizes ($50M–$2B+ seed rounds) that structurally exceed the primary audience's check-size range and check capacity even when the company's base scores are high. The evaluation proceeds under the appropriate profile (typically Profile A with a Gray Zone or Out of Scope — Benchmark flag depending on raise size), but a Fund-Mandate-Fit flag is invoked in Block 1 Market Context Note signaling that the appropriate investor archetype is Multi-Stage Series A Lead at $5M+ check size or out of audience scope entirely. The flag does not change tier assignment; it is documented for triage. Evaluators should not score the AI-Native Frontier classification as a fit problem under any criterion — the fit signal is captured at the scope-flag level.
Target raise falls within the $500K–$15M range. Standard evaluation applies. Target raise exceeds $15M but is at or below $16.5M (10% tolerance). Evaluation proceeds under Profile A with a mandatory acknowledgment that instrument calibration may be less precise. Target raise exceeds $16.5M, or company is publicly traded. Evaluation may proceed as a benchmark exercise if clearly flagged. Scores should not be compared directly to in-scope evaluations. Total raised under $275K with no institutional participation. Evaluation may proceed as a benchmark exercise if clearly flagged.

block.name: Automatic Disqualifiers
block.status: Revised — Tech v1.0 R3; Tech v2.0 R2

section.block:
Tech v1.0 R3: LS v5.1 used 4 disqualifiers (a–d) plus (b-alt) for non-therapeutic data security. The tech rubric expands the list to 10 disqualifiers (a–j) organized in four categories, reflecting tech-specific terminal conditions (founder ownership below 10% post-Seed, IP not assigned, open-source signal manipulation, etc.) that have no LS v5.1 parallel. The 23 research-proposed items were rationalized via an observability filter; items requiring legal diligence (specific liquidation preferences, side-letter provisions, MFN clauses, specific vesting schedule terms) are moved to scored deductions or Block 5 documentation. The Tier 4 (Not Ready) / Out of Scope distinction transfers from LS v5.1 v5.0 R5. Tech v2.0 R2: Added two terminal disqualifiers — (k) Sanctioned Jurisdiction / OFAC-SDN Exposure and (l) Fabricated or Undisclosed Related-Party Customer — in a new fifth category, Regulatory and Customer Integrity, closing the two terminal-stakes coverage gaps identified in Steps 3-4 (sanctions exposure; wholesale customer fabrication). Per the Step 5 Section 5 scoping decision, (l) is written at the wholesale-fabrication bar only — mirroring (g)'s "fabricated wholesale, not when claims are merely inflated" discipline — and explicitly routes inflated (real-but-overstated) customer relationships to the A1/B1 NCSP scored deduction, not to termination. (k) triggers on binary jurisdiction/SDN conditions only. The high bars on (g) and (i) are unchanged; no existing disqualifier (a)-(j) text was altered.
The following conditions trigger automatic disqualification regardless of score. A disqualified company is classified as Out of Scope and does not receive a fundability tier assignment. If any disqualifier is triggered, the evaluation terminates after the Disqualifier Screen (Block 2 of the output format). No criterion scores, total score, or fundability tier are assigned. A score below 40 with no disqualifier triggered is classified as Tier 4 — Not Ready, not as Out of Scope. Out of Scope status is reserved for instrument scope mismatches and disqualifier triggers.
The disqualifiers are organized in four categories below. Mark each as CLEAR, TRIGGERED with explanation, or NOT APPLICABLE where the non-applicability rule applies. Marking NOT APPLICABLE does not trigger disqualification.
Triggering condition: Sporadic, messy, or structurally compromised cap table with unresolved ownership disputes, missing documentation, or legal encumbrances. Refusal to provide a cap table summary by band (founder ownership, investor count, instrument types) when directly asked is itself a triggering condition. Observability: Founder attestation by band; Carta or equivalent cap-table-management tool inspection if disclosed; pattern of refusal across multiple direct questions. Non-applicability: None.
Triggering condition: Founder/CEO ownership below 10% post-Seed, or below 15% post-Series A standards. Excessive prior dilution that signals the founder is no longer aligned with the equity outcome. Observability: Founder attestation by band (founder ownership: >50%, 30–50%, 15–30%, <15%); LTSE or Carta benchmark comparison; cap table summary when available. Non-applicability: None.
Triggering condition: Stacked SAFEs exceeding $3M total combined with no priced round in 24+ months. The stacked-SAFE-plus-stalled-pricing combination indicates material dilution risk and inability to attract a priced lead. Observability: Founder attestation; Crunchbase round history; Walker (Carta) framework for SAFE stack benchmarking; explicit absence of a priced round in the company's funding timeline. Non-applicability: None. SAFE stacks below $3M, or any SAFE stack with a priced round within 24 months, are handled as scored deductions within A5/B5 per the SAFE stack treatment sub-element, not as disqualifiers.
Triggering condition: Intellectual property underlying the company's product is not assigned to the company — for example, IP retained by individual founders without proper assignment agreements; IP retained by a university or prior employer without an exclusive license to the company; IP encumbered by competing claims. Refusal to confirm IP assignment when directly asked is itself a triggering condition. Observability: Founder attestation; standard institutional VC diligence question; refusal to confirm equals trigger. Non-applicability: None.
Triggering condition: Pending or unresolved material litigation that creates existential risk to the company's operations or IP position. Observability: Court records; founder disclosure; news coverage. Non-applicability: None.
Triggering condition: Founder or C-suite executive subject to active SEC enforcement, regulatory enforcement (FTC, DOJ, equivalent), criminal proceedings related to securities fraud or technical misconduct, or equivalent. Observability: Public records (SEC EDGAR, court records, news coverage). Non-applicability: None.
Triggering condition: Founder or executive credentials misrepresented in publicly disclosed materials — fabricated institutional affiliation, false employment history, false educational credentials. Differs from the Negative Credibility Signal Protocol (which applies scored deductions within A1/B1 for minor contradictions): this disqualifier applies only when material credentials are fabricated wholesale, not when claims are merely inflated. Observability: LinkedIn versus employer or university cross-check; reference checks; public records. Non-applicability: None.
Triggering condition: Founder's LinkedIn or equivalent professional record shows current primary employer is not the company being evaluated, indicating part-time or side-project status. Observability: Direct LinkedIn observation; current-employer field. Non-applicability: Some specialized fields (e.g., professor-founders in deep-tech with documented sabbatical or transition timeline) may have legitimate dual-status arrangements at the earliest stages. Mark NOT APPLICABLE with documentation of the transition timeline if a clear path to full-time commitment is published or attested.
Triggering condition: Documented evidence of open-source community-signal manipulation — purchased GitHub stars (CMU research documents $0.03–$0.85/star markets); anomalous star-acquisition velocity curves not matched by commit/issue/PR activity; fake contributor accounts; coordinated star campaigns. The triggering condition requires documented evidence of manipulation, not merely a high star count. Observability: Fork-to-star ratio analysis; star-acquisition velocity curve (star-history.com or equivalent); contributor count and authenticity check; issue/PR activity relative to star count. Non-applicability: Mark NOT APPLICABLE for closed-source companies or companies with no GitHub presence. Marking NOT APPLICABLE does not trigger disqualification.
Triggering condition: Active data security enforcement action — including a consent order, corrective action plan, or equivalent regulatory mandate from a data protection authority (HHS Office for Civil Rights under HIPAA, EU/UK data protection authorities under GDPR, FTC under consumer protection authorities, state attorneys general under state privacy law, or equivalent) — that materially impairs the company's ability to operate, retain customers, or handle regulated data. Observability: Regulatory database (HHS OCR Wall of Shame, FTC enforcement page, EU DPA decisions); public disclosure. Non-applicability: Mark NOT APPLICABLE for tech companies not handling protected health information, genomic data, regulated financial data, or other regulated data categories. Marking NOT APPLICABLE does not trigger disqualification. Mirrors LS v5.1 (b-alt) non-applicability rule.
Triggering condition: The company's primary operating jurisdiction, a named entity in its ownership or control structure, or a named revenue customer cited as a traction signal appears on the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list or an equivalent US sanctions list (e.g., BIS Entity List, SDN sectoral lists); OR the company's stated business model requires processing transactions in or with sanctioned jurisdictions without documented compliance controls (licensing, an OFAC screening program, or equivalent). This is a binary, observable condition determined by a sanctions-list lookup against the stated jurisdiction, owner, or customer; it does not require a judgment about the degree of exposure. The instrument's "globally applicable" scope (Section 1.3) makes this screen necessary to keep that scope internally consistent. Observability: OFAC SDN List search (sanctionssearch.ofac.treas.gov); BIS Entity List; the stated operating jurisdiction; named ownership and customer entities. A direct list match, or a stated model that requires sanctioned-jurisdiction processing without controls, equals a trigger. Non-applicability: Mark NOT APPLICABLE for companies with no cross-border payment exposure, no international revenue, and no named ownership or customer entity in a sanctioned jurisdiction. Marking NOT APPLICABLE does not trigger disqualification. Scored-deduction routing: None. This disqualifier is binary; there is no sub-threshold scored-deduction case. A jurisdiction, owner, or customer is either on a sanctions list (or the model requires sanctioned-jurisdiction processing without controls) or it is not.
Triggering condition: A customer cited as a primary traction signal is (a) demonstrably non-existent — no corroborating record in any independent source (no website, no registration, no third-party reference, no public footprint) after a documented search; or (b) a related party (an investor in the company, a co-founder, a family member, or an entity controlled by the founders or their affiliates) presented as an arm's-length commercial customer without disclosure of the relationship. This disqualifier applies only at the wholesale-fabrication bar — the cited customer either does not exist as claimed, or is a related party misrepresented as independent. It is the customer-claim analog of disqualifier (g)'s wholesale-credential-fabrication standard. Observability: Independent corroboration search for the named customer (corporate registry, website, press coverage, third-party databases); related-party cross-check against the cap table, founder networks, and corporate filings; founder disclosure of customer relationships when directly asked. Non-applicability: Mark NOT APPLICABLE for companies that cite no named customer as a primary traction signal (e.g., pre-revenue companies scored on team and demo). Marking NOT APPLICABLE does not trigger disqualification. Scored-deduction routing (hard boundary from Step 5): Inflated relationships — a real, independent customer whose depth, revenue, or commitment is overstated — are NOT routed here. They are handled as a scored deduction within A1/B1 via the Negative Credibility Signal Protocol (false competitive/traction claim) and within A3/B3 via the revenue-recognition standard. DQ-l terminates only on wholesale fabrication (a non-existent customer) or undisclosed related-party misrepresentation. The inflation-versus-fabrication line stays in the scored layer where a wrong call costs points, not a termination; only the unambiguous fabrication case reaches this terminal gate.
The following conditions are NOT automatic disqualifiers but produce scored deductions within their respective criteria. They are listed here for evaluator routing reference; documentation occurs at the criterion level.
Stacked SAFEs $1M–$3M total without the 24-month no-priced-round combination: A5/B5 band deduction per the SAFE stack treatment sub-element (0.5–2 points depending on stack total). Co-founder departed without proper share repurchase, with departed founder retaining above 10% vested equity: A5/B5 band deduction (1–2 points); flag in Block 5. Missing 83(b) elections when confirmed: A5/B5 band deduction (1 point); cap table cleanup flagged. Non-standard preferred terms from prior rounds (greater-than-1× liquidation preference, participating preferred, super-pro-rata, full-ratchet) when discoverable from founder attestation: A5/B5 band deduction (1–2 points). When only discoverable through full legal diligence, flag in Block 5 only. Toxic prior investors (death-spiral notes, predatory venture debt with warrants, litigation-prone investors): A5/B5 band deduction. AI-Augmented Wrapper with no proprietary data, model work, or workflow lock-in, marketing as "AI-native": handled via A2/B2 AI Modifier (−1 to −2) and A6/B6 force-test deductions. Not a standalone disqualifier. Tier-1 multi-stage seed investor present but explicitly NOT leading the Series A when the round is in market: A5/B5 band deduction (1–2 points); Block 5 risk. Pure software startup with material founder time spent on patent prosecution at Seed: A6/B6 band deduction within Moat criterion (Software application note); not a disqualifier.

section.name: Standardized Scoring Output Format
section.revision_note: Tech v1.0 R11: Output format inherits the seven-block structure from LS v5.1 v5.1 with field-level adaptations for tech context. Block 0 Sector field restructured to four-part format (Primary Sector / Sub-Sector / AI Tier Classification / Business Model). Block 1 Development Stage enumerated list replaces FDA stage values with the tech taxonomy from Section 2.1. Block 1 Routing Rationale required to cite three inputs (RAISE SIZE, DEVELOPMENT STAGE, INVESTOR COMPOSITION) per LS v5.1 R4-05. Block 1 includes routing_input_definitions sub-element with the four-tier investor composition classification. Block 1 Market Context Note format strings added for Fund-Mandate-Fit flag, Wrapper-Risk flag, and Hardware Profile flag. Block 2 Disqualifier Screen restructured with 10 disqualifiers grouped in four categories. Block 3 modifier_sub_block expanded to include AI Tier Classification, AI Modifier value, AI Modifier Justification, M&A Modifier, Combined Modifier (with cap notation), Combined Modifier Justification. Block 4 operational_viability_summary mapping rules adapted for tech anchor criteria. Block 5 Most Likely Investor Archetype field uses defined seven-archetype taxonomy with primary and optional secondary selection.

block.name: Routing Determination
block.revision_note: Tech v2.0 R7: Added a fourth Market Context Note flag string — the Archetype-Misfit flag — that discloses when a company falls outside v2.0's reliable scoring range, defined by four observable triggers (AI-adjacent/frontier-by-research without named-lab pedigree; token or hybrid cap structure; claimed-revenue-only with no verification pathway; novel category with no comps and no strategic partnerships). The trigger list was defined last, after the A1/B1 "or equivalent" (R3) and A3/B3 government-procurement (R5) coverage additions, and it explicitly excludes non-traditional founders and government customers because v2.0 now scores them natively, so the flag fires only on still-uncovered archetypes. The flag is additive: it does not change tier assignment or the Data Confidence machinery, and the existing Fund-Mandate-Fit, Wrapper-Risk, and Hardware flag strings are preserved.

All three inputs are required. Omission of any input is a format error.]

block.routing_input_definitions: INVESTOR COMPOSITION TIER DEFINITIONS: Institutional Series A Lead: Top-tier VC (per A5/B5 Tier 1 lead investor classification) writing ≥50% of round, setting price/terms, taking board seat. Examples: Sequoia, a16z, Founders Fund, Benchmark, Greylock, Conviction (for AI), Boldstart (for infra), YL Ventures (for cyber). Seed-Stage Micro-VC Lead: Recognized seed/early-stage VC (per A5/B5 Tier 2) leading the round. Examples: Hustle Fund, Precursor, Initialized, Floodgate, Cowboy, Forerunner, Uncork, Costanoa, Founder Collective. Accelerator-Anchored: Lead is the accelerator's own fund (YC, Techstars, Sequoia Arc) OR investor base is primarily accelerator-affiliated. Examples: YC SAFE rounds with primarily YC alumni angels; Techstars batch follow-on rounds. Angel Syndicate / Party Round / No Real Lead: No institutional lead per A5/B5 "No Real Lead" definition. Solo angel lead; 10+ angels with no >25% participant; founder-led raise.

scope_flag_definitions.flag: Target raise falls within the $500K–$15M range. Standard evaluation applies.
Target raise exceeds $15M but is at or below $16.5M (10% tolerance). Evaluation proceeds under Profile A with mandatory acknowledgment that instrument calibration may be less precise.
Target raise exceeds $16.5M, or company is publicly traded. Evaluation may proceed as a benchmark exercise if clearly flagged. Scores should not be compared directly to in-scope evaluations.
Total raised under $275K with no institutional participation. Evaluation may proceed as a benchmark exercise if clearly flagged.

scope_flag_unknown_raise_protocol.instruction: If the target raise amount is not publicly disclosed and cannot be confirmed through available sources, assign the Scope Flag as follows: assign "In Scope" with a conditional note if the company's development stage and total capital raised to date are consistent with the $500K–$15M range. Populate the Target Raise field with "[UNCONFIRMED — ROUTING SUBJECT TO REVISION]" and document the assumption explicitly in the Routing Rationale. If the raise target is subsequently confirmed to fall outside the $500K–$15M range or within the $15M–$16.5M Gray Zone, the Scope Flag and Routing Determination must be revised before the evaluation is used for client engagement decisions.

[Optional. For AI-Native Frontier Fund-Mandate-Fit flag: "Market Context Note: AI-Native Frontier classification — Fund-Mandate-Fit flag invoked. Company likely exceeds primary audience check capacity ($500K–$5M). Evaluation proceeds but readers should note that the appropriate investor archetype is Multi-Stage Series A Lead at $5M+ check size or out of audience scope entirely."
For AI-Augmented Wrapper Wrapper-Risk flag: "Market Context Note: AI-Augmented Wrapper classification — Wrapper-Risk flag invoked. Company's AI capability is substantially supplied by third-party APIs. Force-test failure documented in A6/B6 Justification. See Top 3 Fundability Risks."
For Hardware Profile flag: "Market Context Note: Hardware/Deep-Tech application notes applied to A3/B3 (traction certification milestones), A4/B4 (Burn Multiple relaxation), A6/B6 (patent weighting), A2/B2 (Defense/Robotics sector classification). See Future Revisions Log entry FV-tech-1 for deferred Profile C development."
For Archetype-Misfit flag: "Market Context Note: ARCHETYPE-MISFIT — [trigger condition(s)]. Tier assignment is directionally indicative but scoring reliability is reduced for this archetype. Independent verification recommended before engagement decision." Invoke this flag when the company exhibits one or more characteristics that v2.0 does not score natively (i.e., where native scoring has not been established through a Revised criterion in this version): (1) AI-adjacent-infrastructure positioning, or frontier-by-research classification without named-lab pedigree (the v2.0 AI-Native taxonomy has no native slot for these); (2) a token or token/equity-hybrid capital structure (v2.0 A5/B5 language is equity-only); (3) primary revenue reported exclusively as company-claimed metrics with no contract documentation and no independent verification pathway; (4) a novel category with no completed acquisitions in the specific sub-vertical in the trailing 36 months AND no comparable strategic partnerships. Do NOT invoke for: non-traditional founder pedigree (now scored natively per the A1/B1 "or equivalent" equivalences); government/sovereign customers (now scored natively per the A3/B3 government-procurement equivalence note); companies with recognized ARR or documented bookings (addressed by the A3/B3 revenue-recognition standard); or companies clearly classifiable in an existing AI tier (Frontier/Applied/Non-AI/Wrapper). This flag does not change tier assignment and appears alongside any other applicable flags. It measures a different axis from the Data Confidence rating (archetype fit versus data completeness); when invoked, the Data Confidence rating may remain HIGH/MODERATE/LOW per its standard criteria.
Leave blank if no notes are required.]

block.name: Disqualifier Screen
block.revision_note: Tech v2.0 R8: Mirrored the two new Section 2.3 disqualifiers (k) and (l) into the output Disqualifier Screen by adding a fifth category, Regulatory and Customer Integrity, with the corresponding (k) and (l) fields in CLEAR / NOT APPLICABLE / TRIGGERED format, and extended the Disqualifier Outcome NOT-APPLICABLE track to include (k) and (l). The (l) field carries the explicit routing note that inflated (real-but-overstated) customer relationships go to the NCSP scored deduction, not to termination, keeping Section 2.3 and Block 2 identical. No other Block 2 field was altered.
block.instruction:
The disqualifier screen is a gate. If any disqualifier is TRIGGERED, the evaluation terminates here. The company is classified as Out of Scope. No criterion scores, total score, fundability tier, or fundraising readiness are assigned. Blocks 3–5 are populated with "N/A — Disqualified" and the basis for disqualification. Block 6 (Footer) is still completed.
Disqualifiers are organized in four categories. Mark each as CLEAR, TRIGGERED with explanation, or NOT APPLICABLE where the non-applicability rule applies. Marking NOT APPLICABLE does not trigger disqualification.

block.name: Total Score and Tier Determination
block.instruction: Aggregates criterion scores into total score, applies consistency check, assigns fundability tier, and reports operational viability summary.

[Sum of criterion scores using A2/B2 base tier score before combined modifier. Used for tier threshold reconciliation when combined modifier is non-zero.]
[Base score plus applied combined modifier (capped at ±2). Maximum = 102; minimum = 0 for non-disqualified evaluations. Operative envelope = 98-102.]

consistency_check.instruction: Verify internal arithmetic. The Modifier-Adjusted Total Score must equal Base Score plus Combined Modifier. The Combined Modifier must equal AI Modifier plus M&A Modifier capped at ±2. If arithmetic does not reconcile, the evaluation is a format error and must be revised before submission.
consistency_check.field: [Confirm sum of criterion weights = 100. PASS / FAIL with explanation. For Profile A: A1(24)+A2(16)+A3(30)+A4(10)+A5(8)+A6(6)+A7(6) = 100. For Profile B: B1(33)+B2(16)+B3(15)+B4(7)+B5(12)+B6(12)+B7(5) = 100.]

fundability_tier.instruction: Assign tier based on Modifier-Adjusted Total Score per the threshold table below. Out of Scope is reserved for disqualifier triggers and scope mismatches per Sections 2.2 and 2.3, not for low scores.

tier_thresholds.tier: High-velocity fundraising candidate; primary audience deploys; full institutional Series A or Seed path visible; recommended for active pipeline.
Qualified fundraising candidate; secondary audience deploys; pipeline-eligible with documented risks in Top 3 Fundability Risks.
Conditional fundraising candidate; specific risk mitigation required before active engagement; not in primary pipeline.
Not fundraising-ready at current development stage; revisit on milestone achievement.
Disqualifier triggered or scope mismatch per Sections 2.2 and 2.3. No tier assignment.

fundability_tier.field: [Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3 / Tier 4 / Out of Scope — with score and basis]

data_confidence.instruction: Aggregate the per-criterion Data Confidence Flags into an overall rating. Apply the founder-attestation aggregation rule per Section 1.5: when two or more criteria carry INFORMATION-SCARCE flags driven by founder-attestation-only signals, rating moves to MODERATE; when four or more, rating moves to LOW. This rule applies in parallel to the total INSUFFICIENT DATA flag count below.
data_confidence.rating: Two or fewer INSUFFICIENT DATA flags across all criteria; primary evidence is independently observable. Founder-attestation aggregation rule not triggered.

Three to five INSUFFICIENT DATA flags across criteria, OR the founder-attestation aggregation rule is triggered at the 2-criterion threshold. Some scores rest on midpoint-default or founder-attested bands; conclusions are directionally reliable but specific score points are less precise.

Six or more INSUFFICIENT DATA flags across criteria, OR the founder-attestation aggregation rule is triggered at the 4-criterion threshold. Many scores rest on midpoint-default or founder-attested bands; conclusions are directionally indicative but should be confirmed before client-engagement decisions.
data_confidence.field: [HIGH / MODERATE / LOW with brief explanation citing the flag count and any founder-attestation aggregation rule invocation]

operational_viability_summary.instruction: Summarize the operational viability of the company per the A1/A3 (Profile A) or B1/B3 (Profile B) score bands. This summary informs Block 5 Fundraising Outlook and applies regardless of whether the OVC was formally triggered (the OVC trigger is an extreme case of the broader operational viability profile assessment).

mapping_rules.mapping: Both A1/B1 and A3/B3 are in their respective top or upper-mid bands. The company has demonstrated both team viability and product validation. Fundraising path is unobstructed at the operational viability level; success depends on sector tier, market timing, and deal mechanics.

A1/B1 OR A3/B3 (one of the two) is in the lowest band. The company has demonstrated one of the two operational viability dimensions but not the other. Fundraising path is conditional on remediation of the weak dimension. The OVC has not triggered (single condition); but the asymmetric profile is flagged in Top 3 Fundability Risks.

Both A1/B1 AND A3/B3 are in their lowest defined bands. The Operational Viability Condition has triggered and A2/B2 is capped at 8 points (Tier 3 COOL ceiling). The company has not demonstrated minimum operating capacity OR minimum product validation; fundraising path is structurally obstructed regardless of sector tailwinds.

operational_viability_summary.field: [OPERATIONAL / MARGINAL / PRE-OPERATIONAL with citation of A1/B1 and A3/B3 band assignments]

fundraising_readiness.instruction: Mapping of fundability tier and operational viability status to a fundraising readiness narrative for the client engagement decision.

mapping_rule.mapping: Ready for active pipeline. Strong-fit candidate with operational viability confirmed. Engagement priority: high.
Pipeline-eligible with documented risks. Engagement priority: medium; risk mitigation discussed before client engagement.
Conditional engagement. Specific risk mitigation required; pipeline placement deferred pending milestone achievement.

mapping.tier: Tier 4 or any tier with PRE-OPERATIONAL viability

mapping_rule.mapping: Not ready for active engagement. Revisit on documented milestone achievement (operational viability remediation or score band advancement).
No fundraising readiness assessment. Disqualifier or scope flag governs.

fundraising_readiness.field: [1 to 2 sentences citing the tier, the operational viability status, and the recommended engagement priority.]

block.name: Qualitative Assessment
block.instruction: Provides the qualitative complement to the quantitative scoring. Required for every non-disqualified evaluation. Each field must be populated with content specific to the evaluation; placeholder text is a format error.

top_3_fundability_strengths.instruction: Identify the three strongest fundraising signals from the evaluation. Each strength must cite the underlying criterion and observable evidence. Strengths are framed in terms of fundraising appeal to the target investor archetype, not product or technical merit.
top_3_fundability_strengths.field: [1 to 3 sentences naming the strength, citing the criterion (A1/B1 through A7/B7), and identifying the observable evidence.]
[1 to 3 sentences naming the strength, citing the criterion, and identifying the observable evidence.]
[1 to 3 sentences naming the strength, citing the criterion, and identifying the observable evidence.]

top_3_fundability_risks.instruction: Identify the three most material fundraising risks from the evaluation. Each risk must cite the underlying criterion and observable evidence. Risks are framed in terms of investor concerns at deal velocity assessment, not product or technical risk. Cross-criterion risks (a single development affecting multiple criteria simultaneously per Section 1.7 cross-criterion symmetry) must be flagged here with the correlated criteria identified.
top_3_fundability_risks.field: [1 to 3 sentences naming the risk, citing the criterion or criteria affected, and identifying the observable evidence. Cross-criterion correlations stated explicitly when applicable.]
[1 to 3 sentences naming the risk, citing the criterion or criteria affected, and identifying the observable evidence.]
[1 to 3 sentences naming the risk, citing the criterion or criteria affected, and identifying the observable evidence.]

fundraising_outlook.instruction: Synthesizes the evaluation into a forward-looking narrative covering: (a) the most likely investor archetype that will lead the round; (b) the expected timeline and process dynamics; (c) the key risks to closing. The Most Likely Investor Archetype field is populated by selecting from the seven-archetype taxonomy defined below. A primary archetype is required; a secondary archetype is optional when two distinct paths are visible.

investor_archetypes.archetype: Small-fund seed VC ($50M-$200M fund size) with deep sector specialization (e.g., YL Ventures for cybersecurity; Conviction for AI; Boldstart for infrastructure; Founders Fund for defense/deep-tech). Writes $1M-$5M Seed checks. Sector specialization and follow-on capacity within the target sector are the primary fit signals. Best fit: Profile B companies in PEAK or ACTIVE sectors with sector-aligned founder pedigree and credible moat-buildability trajectory.

Generalist micro-VC ($50M-$300M fund size) without strict sector mandate (e.g., Hustle Fund, Precursor, Initialized, Floodgate, Forerunner, Founder Collective). Writes $500K-$3M Seed checks. Team quality and Founder-Market Fit clarity are the primary fit signals; sector tier is secondary. Best fit: Profile B companies with strong team signals across sectors.

Specialist AI fund or AI-focused vertical ($100M-$500M fund size; e.g., Conviction, Radical Ventures, Air Street, AI Grant). Writes $2M-$10M checks at upper Seed through Series A. AI-Native classification (Frontier or Applied), proprietary model work or data flywheel, and frontier-lab founder pedigree are the primary fit signals. Best fit: AI-Native Applied or AI-Native Frontier companies at Profile A or upper Profile B with strong AI moat-buildability.

Top-tier multistage VC ($500M+ fund size; e.g., Sequoia, a16z, Founders Fund, Benchmark, Greylock, Kleiner, Accel). Writes $5M-$15M Series A checks with documented follow-on capacity through Series B and beyond. Board seat mandatory; price/term setting required. Best fit: Profile A companies with Tier 1 lead investor profile, $1M+ ARR for Non-AI SaaS or $500K+ ARR for AI-Native Applied, and strong moat existence. AI-Native Frontier companies raising at $50M+ valuations route to this archetype regardless of Block 1 raise size (per Section 2.2 Fund-Mandate-Fit scope boundary).

Sector specialist fund focused on defense, dual-use, and national-security technology (e.g., Founders Fund defense vertical, Lux Capital, Shield Capital, America's Frontier Fund, In-Q-Tel via strategic vehicle). Writes $2M-$15M checks across Seed and Series A. Defense/dual-use sector classification, security-cleared founder pedigree, government contract revenue, and ITAR/EAR-protected IP are the primary fit signals. Best fit: defense or dual-use companies regardless of profile, including hardware-intensive companies under the Profile Limitation framework.

Accelerator's own fund participating in the post-accelerator round (Y Combinator continuity fund, Techstars continuity, Sequoia Arc, a16z Speedrun follow-on). Writes $250K-$2M checks at Seed. Tier 1 or Tier 2 accelerator membership is a structural prerequisite. Best fit: Profile B companies with active Tier 1 or Tier 2 accelerator participation and strong batch peer-fundraising momentum.

Angel syndicate (AngelList syndicates, Sweetwater) or solo GP fund ($10M-$100M fund size). Writes $100K-$1M checks. Founder-Market Fit and personal-network endorsement are the primary fit signals; institutional rigor is lower. Best fit: Profile B companies at Pre-Product through Pre-Revenue Public Beta stages with strong founder credibility but limited institutional traction.

fundraising_outlook.field: [Select one from the seven-archetype taxonomy above. State the archetype name and one-sentence justification citing the criteria that anchor the fit (typically A1/B1 team, A2/B2 sector tier and AI Tier, A5/B5 lead investor quality).]

[Optional. Select one from the seven-archetype taxonomy when two distinct fundraising paths are visible (e.g., AI-Focused Early-Stage VC primary + Multi-Stage Series A Lead secondary for an AI-Native Applied company at the Profile A/B boundary). Leave blank if only one path is visible.]

[1 to 2 sentences describing expected fundraising timeline from active outreach to close, citing development stage, sector tier, AI tier, and any flags (Fund-Mandate-Fit, Wrapper-Risk) that compress or extend the timeline.]

[1 to 3 sentences identifying the key risks to closing the round. Cross-reference Top 3 Fundability Risks and note any cross-criterion correlations per Section 1.7. SCA severe contradictions and PRE-OPERATIONAL viability status must be cited here when applicable.]

block.name: Evaluation Footer
block.instruction: Required for every evaluation including disqualified evaluations. Provides closure metadata and auditability anchors.
block.field: [1 to 3 sentences summarizing the overall conclusion: tier assignment (or Out of Scope basis), operational viability status, primary investor archetype, and the recommended engagement decision.]

[PASS / FAIL with explanation. PASS confirms: (a) all required Block 0 through Block 6 fields populated; (b) routing rationale cites all three required inputs; (c) SCA documentation present in A5/B5 Justification; (d) NCSP documentation present in A1/B1 Justification; (e) modifier sub-block populated for A2/B2; (f) weight arithmetic reconciles per Block 4 consistency check; (g) midpoint-default justifications meet the standard in Section 1.5.]
[YYYY-MM-DD — optional, populated if a post-engagement audit is scheduled]
